transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sofia Kim (Redwood CSM); Priya Sharma (Hashline CTO), Evan Cole (ML Eng), Jorge Rivera (DevOps), Maya Singh (Security)

Summary (auto):
Initial discovery for Hashline Labs' plan to move away from existing hosted provider and evaluate Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key themes: model compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks, eval parity with OpenAI endpoints, security (KMS, audit logs, SSO), latency vs cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps for security docs, benchmark runbook, and demo account.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points
- Model serving (vLLM/TGI) compatibility
- Private deployment / VPC constraints
- Security and compliance needs (KMS, SSO, SOC2)
- Benchmarking and eval parity plan

Action items (quick list):
- Redwood: send compliance pack, pricing, and runbook
- Hashline: provide prompt set and traffic profile

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is lena from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE for Hashline, with me is marco our solutions engineer and sofia in customer success. how are you doing?
[00:07] Priya Sharma: doing well, thanks. appreciate you fitting us in. quick context — we're Hashline Labs, we run a recommendation and content generation platform, currently on a mix of OpenAI hosted APIs and our self-hosted vLLM cluster for cost reasons. we're exploring an escape hatch — move to a single vendor to simplify ops.
[00:25] Lena Park: awesome, that's the right framing. can you walk us through the stack and what's driving the move?
[00:30] Priya Sharma: yeah so, we have about 120k queries/day, bursty traffic to 400k during morning syncs. primary model family is a custom-tuned Llama derivative via vLLM in-house, and we also call OpenAI for a few specialty finetunes because of latency and perf we couldn't match. main pain points are cost unpredictability on OpenAI, the ops overhead of maintaining vLLM and inconsistent latency, and compliance — some customers need data residency and audit trails.
[00:58] Marco Diaz: when you say vLLM cluster, are you running TGI or the original vllm repo?
[01:02] Evan Cole: it's a mix — we've got vLLM for lower-latency batching and a small TGI setup for certain pipelines, to be honest it's a bit of a Frankenstein.
[01:09] Marco Diaz: okay that helps. typical questions we'll look at: model format compatibility, how KV cache/prefix caching maps across runtimes, and whether your prompt engineering and evals will produce parity when we replace paths that currently hit OpenAI.
[01:22] Jorge Rivera: right, and from infra side we need to understand network topologies — do you support customer VPC peering, private endpoints, and how are keys managed.
[01:31] Sofia Kim: we do both hosted and private options — Redwood Hosted is quickest to get started; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools; Private gives your VPC/on-prem setup with customer-managed networking and KMS integrations.
[01:41] Maya Singh: security first question, do you have SOC2 and can we get audit logs for every API call? also want to know about KMS/HSM integration for key custody.
[01:50] Marco Diaz: yes to SOC2 — we'll send the certs. audit logs are available per-token and per-request; you can route logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder. KMS integrations include AWS KMS and common HSM gateways — for Private you can bring-your-own KMS.
[02:06] Priya Sharma: what's the typical latency for hosted vs Dedicated? our SLOs are 200–250ms p50 for short form completions and under 1.2s p95 for multi-turn conversation flows.
[02:17] Lena Park: latency depends on model size and batching. for smaller Llama variants on our Hosted cluster p50s are often ~80–150ms with light load; Dedicated gives more predictable tail latency and isolated pools for consistent p95. Private depends on your infra but we provide kernel selection and runtime tuning for vLLM/TGI-like paths.
[02:34] Evan Cole: is the inference runtime the same as vLLM? like, can we drop in our current checkpoints and expect identical caching behavior?
[02:40] Marco Diaz: the runtime is Redwood's GPU-optimized engine, not vLLM. it supports similar KV cache semantics and continuous batching. we do sometimes see small behavioral differences — e.g., attention kernel numerics can cause 0.1–0.5% output drift. that's why we run eval parity.
[02:54] Priya Sharma: that drift is fine if we can measure it and ensure no regression, esp for our scoring models. what's your parity process?
[03:00] Marco Diaz: we run a two-stage parity: first functional parity with your prompt set for n-perplexity/metrics and human evals on a sampled subset; then perf parity for latency/cost with mirrored traffic. we capture token-for-token diffs and produce a regression dashboard.
[03:15] Lena Park: and we can fallback — routing policies can call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint if we detect regressions during rollout.
[03:22] Jorge Rivera: talk to me about deployment. for Private, do you require a private control plane talking to our VPC? data plane stays inside?
[03:30] Marco Diaz: yes, control plane can be managed by Redwood but customer can opt for private control plane in your VPC. data plane and model weights remain inside your network for Private/on-prem installs.
[03:39] Maya Singh: encryption at rest? models must be encrypted.
[03:42] Marco Diaz: encrypted at rest with KMS, and HSM option for key custody.
[03:46] Priya Sharma: how hard is it to ingest our existing checkpoints — we have some sharded LoRA finetunes and custom tokenizer artifacts.
[03:54] Marco Diaz: we accept standard PyTorch/transformers checkpoints, adapters/LoRA are supported in Dedicated and Private; tokenizer artifacts may need a small compatibility shim — we'll take a look during onboarding.
[04:03] Evan Cole: we rely heavily on persistent KV cache between sessions for fast chat—will that survive?
[04:07] Marco Diaz: yes, we support persistent KV cache and prefix caching; for Hosted we have configurable TTLs, for Dedicated you can have isolated cache stores with guaranteed eviction policies.
[04:16] Priya Sharma: pricing — can you ballpark how Dedicated compares to our current spend? we spend about $55k/month split across OpenAI and infra.
[04:25] Lena Park: ballpark depends on model mix and throughput — we can model it once you share prompt set and token distribution. generally customers see 20–40% lower unit cost when moving to Dedicated with quantization and batching optimizations.
[04:37] Priya Sharma: any red flags around vendor lock-in? we want to be able to move back if needed.
[04:42] Lena Park: portability is a core focus — you can pin model versions and we support both OpenAI-compatible APIs and raw model access. for Private you keep model weights and can always move them. we also provide exportable prompts and evals.
[04:54] Jorge Rivera: our networking team wants to validate peering, firewall rules — can you provide a secure topology diagram?
[04:59] Sofia Kim: yes we'll send a topoloy + connection guide.
[05:02] Priya Sharma: about benchmarks — evan and i want to run a vLLM vs Redwood parity test for our top 50 prompts. how invasive is that?
[05:11] Marco Diaz: not invasive — we can run isolated bench instances and mirror traffic. we'll need your prompt set, a representative payload size distribution, and any finetunes. we'll run locally in your VPC for Private or in a sandbox on Dedicated/Hosted depending on preference.
[05:23] Evan Cole: do you support streaming and function calls like OpenAI? we use streaming heavily for real-time UI.
[05:28] Marco Diaz: yes, streaming responses and tool/function calling primitives are supported; slight differences in chunking may appear but we can align.
[05:35] Lena Park: quick clarifying question — are there regulatory constraints for EU or APAC data residency?
[05:40] Priya Sharma: EU customers require data to stay in-region, and we have a couple of APAC clients. ideally want region pinning for both logs and inference.
[05:49] Marco Diaz: region pinning is supported for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private you'd deploy to the region you control. we'll note that for the runbook.
[05:56] Maya Singh: one more security nit — SSO and RBAC. We need SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC on model endpoints.
[06:03] Marco Diaz: SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported; RBAC down to route/model level is available in Dedicated and Private.
[06:10] Priya Sharma: what's the timeline to get a proof-of-concept? we want to decide in 6–8 weeks.
[06:15] Lena Park: doable — typical POC is 2–4 weeks for parity runs plus a 1–2 week decisioning period. we'll aim to have security docs and demo ready within a week so you can sign the NDA and get the sandbox.
[06:26] Evan Cole: can you also surface typical issues you see in portouts? any gotchas?
[06:31] Marco Diaz: common ones: tokenizer differences, finetune adapter loading (LoRA mapping), and subtle numeric differences causing ranking shifts. we mitigate with evals, rollback policies, and compatibility shims.
[06:42] Priya Sharma: okay that makes sense.
[06:44] Jorge Rivera: ops question — how do you handle autoscaling and burst capacity? our traffic spikes are unpredictable.
[06:50] Lena Park: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling with reserved base capacity and burst pools; Hosted has shared burst capacity. For strict SLAs you'd go Dedicated or Private with burst policies.
[07:02] [crosstalk] Maya Singh: sorry —
[07:03] Priya Sharma: go ahead maya.
[07:04] Maya Singh: just to confirm — audit retention windows are configurable? we need 7 years for audit logs for some contracts.
[07:09] Marco Diaz: long-term retention can be done via log export to your S3 or SIEM; we'll discuss retention costs in the pricing sheet.
[07:17] Lena Park: okay let's recap and cement next steps. we'll: 1) send SOC2 & ISO docs + network topology guide, 2) provide Dedicated sizing and pricing template, 3) Marco will send benchmark runbook and ask-for-data list, 4) Hashline to share prompt set and traffic CSV. Is that a fair list?
[07:36] Priya Sharma: yes, looks good. also add proposed dates for the parity kickoff.
[07:40] Lena Park: noted. any other blockers?
[07:43] Evan Cole: just curious — are there any customers who ported from OpenAI and ran parity with vLLM? want a short case study.
[07:51] Sofia Kim: we have a mid-market finserv customer who ran a TGI parity test, reduced per-token cost ~35% and kept subjective quality within acceptable threshold — i'll include an anonymized snippet.
[08:01] Priya Sharma: perfect.
[08:03] Lena Park: great. we'll send the materials by end of day tomorrow. we'll propose 2026-05-06 for the parity kickoff, unless that conflicts.
[08:12] Priya Sharma: that works. thanks everyone.
[08:15] Lena Park: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc bundle. talk soon.
[08:19] [meeting end]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (vLLM as v-lum, TGI as tee-gee-eye) and minor speaker mislabels. Natural speech patterns and interruptions preserved.
